# `Q-5-28` — llms-txt Would Overwrite an Existing File

> `website.llms-txt: true` wants to write a file that already exists
> in the output directory and was not generated by llms-txt.
> Overwriting it silently would destroy that content.

## What this means

When `llms-txt` is enabled, Quarto writes three kinds of files into
the output directory alongside your rendered pages:

- a markdown companion next to every page (`about.html` gets
  `about.md`),
- `llms.txt`, an organized index of those companions, and
- `llms-full.txt`, all companions concatenated.

These paths share a namespace with your own files. If a copied
resource — or any file already sitting in the output directory —
occupies one of them, Quarto refuses to overwrite it and fails the
render instead:

```yaml
# _quarto.yml
project:
  type: website
  resources:
    - about.md        # copied to _site/about.md …

website:
  llms-txt: true      # … which is also about.html's companion path
```

Quarto tracks the files it generated in previous renders (in
`.quarto/llms-manifest.json`), so re-renders update its own output
freely; only files it cannot prove are its own are protected.

## How to fix it

Pick whichever matches your intent:

- **Rename or move the conflicting file** so the companion path is
  free.
- **Drop it from `project.resources`** (or delete it from the output
  directory, if it was left behind by something else).
- **Disable the feature** with `website.llms-txt: false` if you'd
  rather ship your own hand-written files at these paths.

## Why an error and not a warning

The same policy as alias redirects ([Q-5-24](Q-5-24.qmd)): a build
that silently replaces one file's content with another's ships wrong
content with no signal. Failing the render costs a rename; the
silent overwrite costs a page.
